"skipFiles": ["${workspaceFolder}/node_modules/**", "<node_internals>/**"]

Q: Invariant Violation: TurboModuleRegistry.getEnforcing(...): 'RNGestureHandlerModule' A:

If you're using iOS and installing react-native-gesture-handler for the first time, make sure you kill the app in Xcode and rebuild it from there. Just reloading the app by running yarn react-native start --reset-cache is not sufficient to get a fully rebuilt app with the necessary RNGestureHandlerModule module installed.

Q: Use svg image as map layer for mapbox GL JS A:

As Far as I know, Mapbox-gl-js does not support to add SVG as layer(Github Link), You have to do some workaround using external Libraries/tools like D3 and possible duplicate Link and reason why it is throwing error is because SVG has pixel coordinates and gl-js deals with geographical coordinates(Lat/Lng)

Q: How to connect multiple services without creating direct dependencies between them? A:

Setting up events and event listeners isn't that tricky, but if you want to make your life a little easier, you could use out-of-the-box Roblox objects. You could use one or many BindableEvents stored somewhere like ServerScriptStorage or ReplicatedStorage.

BindableEvents are good for communicating from one server side script to another, or from one client side script to another. (If you need client to server communication, use a RemoteEvent)

Your services would bind to the relevant Event RbxScriptSignal. One example based on one of your StageBehaviors would be something like...

-- locate your BindableEvent
local CharacterSpawnedOnStageEvent : BindableEvent = game.ServerScriptStorage.StageBehaviors.CharacterSpawnedOnStage

-- listen for when the event fires
local connection = CharacterSpawnedOnStageEvent.Event:Connect(function(player : Player)
    print("A player has been spawned on the stage :", player.Name)
end)

Then a different service would tell the BindableEvent to fire when that thing happened...

-- locate your BindableEvent
local CharacterSpawnedOnStageEvent : BindableEvent = game.ServerScriptStorage.StageBehaviors.CharacterSpawnedOnStage

game.Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player : Player)
    player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(character : Model)
        -- the character has been added to the world, tell the other services...
        CharacterSpawnedOnStageEvent:Fire(player)
    end)
end)

This way, your services aren't binding to each other, but rather to shared BindableEvents that exist in your game. This allows any service to dispatch events to them, and any other service to listen to those events.

Q: Programming| System Development A:

A structured web app development process usually follows these stages:

1. Requirement Analysis – Gather requirements, understand the target users, define the project scope, and set clear goals.

2. UI/UX Design – Create wireframes, mockups, and prototypes to plan the user experience and interface before development begins.

3. Frontend Development – Build the user-facing part of the application using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and frameworks such as React, Angular, or Vue.

4. Backend Development – Develop server-side logic, APIs, authentication, and database management using technologies like Node.js, Django, Spring Boot, or Flask.

5. Data Design base– Design and optimize the database structure to ensure efficient data storage and retrieval.

6. Testing & Quality Assurance – Perform unit testing, integration testing, system testing, and user acceptance testing to ensure reliability and functionality.

7. Deployment – Deploy the application to production using cloud platforms, hosting services, and CI/CD pipelines for automated releases.

8. Maintenance & Scaling – Monitor performance, fix bugs, apply security updates, and scale infrastructure as the user base grows.

This framework provides a complete lifecycle for web application development, from initial planning to long-term maintenance and optimization.
